lines: By Sol 1,847 the colony had stopped asking Imani why she wasted water on tomatoes.
But every evening, when the dust storms painted the dome orange, she walked the rows of the little greenhouse with a watering can older than the settlement, and talked to the plants.
The children called it Imani's church.
She called it nothing; it was only that she had grown up in Kumasi, where her grandmother greeted every tree by name, and she could not imagine a garden with nobody to say hello.
On Sol 1,848 the last supply ship was cancelled.
On Sol 1,849 the first tomato ripened, red as a small, defiant heart.
She carried it, with both hands, to the airlock where the children were pressed against the glass, watching the storm, and put it in the smallest hand she could find.
